title: Variables & Data Types
description: Learn about different data types and how to convert between them.

lessons.title: Understanding Data Types
lessons.content: JavaScript data types define the kind of data a variable can hold. These include primitive types such as String, Number, Boolean, Null, Undefined, and Symbol. Recognizing data types is fundamental to predict how operations on values will behave.

lessons.title: Primitive vs Reference Types
lessons.content: Primitive data types store actual values, while reference types store memory addresses pointing to objects or arrays. This distinction affects how data is copied and manipulated, influencing behavior during assignment and function calls.

lessons.title: Declaring Variables with let and const
The String Data Type
Numbers and Numeric Precision
lessons.content: JavaScript uses the IEEE 754 standard for numeric values, representing all numbers as floating-point values. This can lead to precision issues with decimals, requiring careful handling in financial or scientific calculations.

lessons.title: Booleans and Logical Values
lessons.content: Boolean values represent truthiness — either `true` or `false`. They are essential in controlling program flow, especially in conditional statements and loops.

lessons.title: Null vs Undefined
lessons.content: `null` is an intentional absence of any object value, often used to reset variables. `undefined` means a variable has been declared but not assigned a value yet, indicating uninitialized state.

lessons.title: Type Conversion
Type Coercion
lessons.content: JavaScript performs implicit type conversion (type coercion) when operators involve mismatched data types. While convenient, this can sometimes cause unexpected results, so understanding coercion rules helps avoid bugs.

lessons.title: Checking Data Types
lessons.content:
console.log(typeof 'hello'); // string
console.log(typeof 123); // number
console.log(typeof true); // boolean
// The `typeof` operator helps verify the type of any variable or value.
